A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, algorithms, and figures. V6's main-text proofs and related work can be matched to v7's Appendices A–D.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 1–2 report original numerical experiments on cubic-regularized bilinear problems and AUC maximization using three LIBSVM datasets.

after.justification: Section 5 retains the original synthetic and AUC experiments and reports additional synthetic problem dimensions in Figure 1.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3 retain their regularized updates, inexactness conditions, sampling rules, and Schur-based Newton–bisection routine. The added scalar-tolerance derivation explains enforcement of the existing Condition 4.2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same cubic-regularized bilinear task and AUC maximization on a9a, covtype, and w8a. The added synthetic dimensions change problem sizes within retained coverage.

E2.justification: Synthetic comparisons retain EG1, OGDA1, EG2 from Bullins and Lai, and OGDA2 from Jiang and Mokhtari. AUC comparisons retain SEG and SVREG. No comparator is added or removed within either experiment.

E3.justification: Figure 1 adds n = 20, 500, and 1000 to the original n = 50, 100, and 200, retaining rho = 1/(20n). The AUC inner-solver specification changes from Newton to safeguarded Newton–bisection/Newton variants, without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The expanded Figure 1 extends the existing problem-size analysis and supports discussion of stability and scalability through n = 1000. The new hyperparameter discussion explicitly defers systematic sensitivity sweeps; it does not report new hyperparameter or Jacobian-noise ablations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The subsampling probability bounds and experimental delta = 0.01 setting are retained.

E6.justification: Figure 1 adds results for three dimensions and revises timing curves for retained dimensions. The new n = 500 comparison shows OGDA2 ahead of the proposed method in both iteration and time plots. Figure 2's AUC curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: V7 Section 4.2 newly derives the identity connecting the nonlinear residual to the scalar root residual and an explicit sufficient tolerance for Condition 4.2, establishing finite inner termination. The main assumptions, convergence theorems, and relocated proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The core contributions, O(epsilon^(-2/3)) iteration guarantee, and Schur-decomposition complexity advantage are retained. The abstract now specifies AUC/LIBSVM and comparative practical efficiency, but these experiments and findings already appear in v6.

C2.justification: V7 substantially expands practical limitations: estimating the Hessian Lipschitz bound, quadratic factor-storage requirements, suitability for moderate dimensions, hyperparameter cost tradeoffs, and missing noise-sensitivity and quasi-Newton comparisons. Section 5 also qualifies earlier outperformance language as competitive and often faster on tested instances.

D1.justification: Remark 2.7 newly discloses that AUC gap calculations use a best-found solution as a proxy; this documents the existing evaluation without establishing a protocol change. V7 also adds root-stopping guidance and states shared hyperparameter defaults. Hardware, MATLAB version, and dataset access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged, and v6 Section 1.1 is retained as Appendix A. Expanded discussion of Chen et al. reiterates the existing positioning around practical explicit methods versus faster but more involved nested procedures.

P1.justification: V7 substantially reorganizes the narrative by moving related work to Appendix A and detailed proofs to Appendices B–D. It condenses notation and convergence material, rewrites the contribution discussion, and adds substantial practical explanation around the algorithms and experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 1 expands from a two-by-three to a four-by-three panel arrangement, with additional dimension panels and revised time axes. Figure 2 retains its six-panel display. Several algorithm and equation displays are also compacted during the reorganization.

improvement.justification: V7 improves practical clarity through the stopping-tolerance derivation, disclosure of the AUC reference-solution proxy, and more qualified efficiency and scalability conclusions alongside the expanded Figure 1. Proofs remain available in the appendices. These gains are limited by incomplete proxy tolerance/budget details and an inconsistent synthetic setup paragraph that still lists only the original three dimensions.
